Low
fertility
is
a
concern
for
many
OECD
countries
as
they
face
the
prospect
of
population
ageing
.
This
article
makes
comparisons
between
Australia
and
seven
other
OECD
countries
in
fertility
rates
between
1970
and
2004
.
Changing
age
patterns
of
fertility
are
also
compared
and
show
that
for
most
of
the
countries
,
women
are
postponing
childbirth
and
having
fewer
babies
.
The
associations
of
women's
education
levels
and
rates

are
also
explored
